Two changes are correct: starting at start+1 and including `end`, and handling end < start by swapping and negating. Together they pass 8 of the 9 tests. The `has_weekend_holiday` / `end_condition` logic is a hack aimed at one test. It drops the end date whenever ANY holiday in the list falls on a weekend, even one far outside the range. For example, (Mon, Tue, [a distant Saturday]) returns 0 instead of 1. It also contradicts the docstring, which says weekend holidays "remove nothing and are not moved to a nearby weekday."

The underlying problem is that test_july_fourth_week_2026 conflicts with the docstring. July 4, 2026 is a Saturday, so 2026-06-29 → 2026-07-06 is 5 business days under the documented rule (Jun 30, Jul 1–3, Jul 6). The test expects 4, which only works if the holiday moves to Fri, Jul 3 (the US observed rule). No correct implementation can satisfy both the test and the docstring.

Please remove the weekend-holiday hack and keep the correct loop and negative-range fix. Since the teammate asked not to change the tests, raise the conflict with them and the fulfilment team. Either the test should expect 5 (or pass the observed date, 2026-07-03), or the spec really does move weekend holidays and the docstring and implementation should change on purpose. Also add a PR description that explains this.
